Questions.question: Where was Farhan when his mistake happened?
What caused Farhan’s incorrect connection?
Questions.answer: He read the label too quickly.
options: He read the label too quickly.

Questions.question: Where was Thenu during her mistake?
Why were Thenu’s readings inaccurate?
Questions.answer: She held the probes too loosely.
options: She used the wrong voltage scale.
She held the probes too loosely.

activity_b.text: Farhan and Thenu walked up to Ms. Brown after the morning safety briefing.
Both looked slightly nervous, and Farhan spoke first.
Good morning, Madam, we need to talk to you.
We realised we made a few mistakes last week, and we want to explain them properly.
Ayubowan, both of you. Thank you for coming to me directly.
Let’s go through them one by one.
Farhan, tell me then, what happened?
I connected the wrong circuit to the breaker.
Where exactly were you when your problem occurred?
I was near the distribution board, right beside the cable-routing tray.
And when did it happen? What time was it?
It was Tuesday, around ten thirty, just before the safety inspection.
Alright. Now tell me—how did you end up connecting the wrong circuit to the breaker?
Madam… I read the label too quickly.
I should have checked the wiring diagram first, but I didn’t.
I usually check diagrams, but not every morning—maybe two or three times a week.
And why didn’t you check it that morning?
Honestly, Madam, I thought the labels were still correct from the previous job.
But now I understand that I must double-check everything.
Good. So how will you make sure this doesn’t happen again?
I’m going to check the diagram every morning, confirm the labels, and trace each wire slowly before connecting anything.
Alright. Now, Thenu, what was your mistake?
The first readings of the voltage were inaccurate.
Where were you when your mistake happened?
I was near the inverter panel, right beside the multimeter rack.
And when was that?
Friday around 2.45 p.m., during the voltage-testing session.
And how did your first set of readings become so inaccurate?
Madam, I set the multimeter correctly, but I placed the probes too loosely and didn’t hold them steady.
I also used the older probe set, and the contact point wasn’t clean.
Why didn’t you check the probes?
I was rushing, Madam.
I check them most of the time, but that day I hurried because I thought the next test would take long.
So how will you avoid this next time?
I’m going to clean the probe tips, secure the contacts properly, and use the newer set for testing.
I’ll also take my time with each reading.
Good. These are small mistakes—not big failures—but they matter.
Let’s stay consistent this week.
